title: Why ChatGPT Makes Things Up: AI Hallucinations Explained 🤥 #shorts
description:
AI chatbots sometimes state things that are completely false, with total confidence. That's a hallucination. A language model doesn't look facts up: it predicts the most likely next word, one word at a time. When it hasn't seen the answer, it still produces something that sounds right. Grounding it in real documents (RAG), asking for sources and checking important facts all reduce the risk.

📘 More to learn + my projects: https://github.com/HemashreeVI

#AI #ChatGPT #LLM #AIHallucination #GenerativeAI #TechExplained #shorts

lines: Ask an AI for a book, and it might give you a perfect title, author and year. For a book that doesn't exist.
A language model doesn't look anything up. It predicts the most likely next word, one word at a time.
When it has never seen the real answer, it doesn't stop. It keeps predicting words that sound right, and sounding right isn't the same as being right.
And it says the made-up answer in exactly the same confident tone as a true one.
The fixes: give it real documents to answer from, ask it for sources, and double check anything important.
It predicts words, not facts. Always verify.
